# Competitive analysis: compare UX patterns, features and gaps across rival products

Curated by Skill Harbor — @owl-listener's competitive-analysis UX skill: a systematic framework for evaluating the competitive landscape from a design perspective. Runs four steps: competitor identification (direct — same problem, same audience; indirect — same problem, different audience; aspirational benchmarks from adjacent domains), evaluation across seven dimensions (information architecture, interaction patterns, visual design, content strategy, performance, accessibility, mobile experience), a feature comparison matrix (per key task: support level, steps required, UX quality 1-5, unique approaches), and strengths/weaknesses/opportunities (what each excels at, friction points, table-stakes patterns, unaddressed gaps). Deliverables: summary overview, comparison matrix, competitor profiles, opportunity map, annotated references. Best practices: focus on UX quality not just feature presence, analyze full journeys not isolated screens, update regularly, include aspirational examples from outside the category. Honest caveats: methodology only, no tooling; for deliberately adopting rivals' conventions, the skill points to a `jakobs-law` skill that is not bundled here. MIT licensed. Sibling skills from the same repo are listed separately: « owl-listener-designer-skills-error-handling-ux » and « owl-listener-designer-skills-metrics-definition ». Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use. Discovered via skills.sh.
